title: Fever, 150 and frightened
objective: Treat thyroid storm -- fever, tachycardia, agitation, confusion, vomiting, diarrhea -- as an emergency needing immediate care and treatment of the cause

brief.situation: 15:00 on a surgical unit. You are Ms. Okoye's nurse. She is 38, on day 1 after an emergency appendectomy. She has Graves disease and stopped her methimazole a month ago because she 'felt fine'. She is restless and sweating and says her heart is racing.
handover: At 11:00: temperature 37.9 C, heart rate 104. She vomited at lunch and has had loose stools since.
PRN orders: acetaminophen or aspirin for fever (order set); lorazepam for anxiety.
Unit policy: call the rapid response team for a heart rate over 130, new confusion, or a temperature over 39.5 C; the RN starts cooling measures while waiting.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each assessment takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: What is happening to Ms. Okoye, what set it off, and what do you do now?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: Thyroid storm: very high fever, tachycardia with atrial fibrillation, agitation and confusion, vomiting and diarrhea; precipitated by stopping methimazole and by surgery; a true emergency with high mortality.
parts.modelAnswer: This is thyroid storm. She has Graves, stopped her methimazole a month ago and had surgery yesterday. Fever over 40, a heart rate around 150 and irregular, new confusion, vomiting and diarrhea. It's an emergency and it can kill her.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Calls rapid response now; cools with blankets off, a cooling blanket and acetaminophen, never aspirin; does not sedate and wait; gives the ordered beta-blocker and fluids; ICU transfer; the thionamide comes before any iodine.
parts.modelAnswer: Call rapid response now and start cooling with acetaminophen, not aspirin, because aspirin can raise free thyroid hormone. Don't just sedate her. Give the ordered beta-blocker and fluids and get her to the ICU, where she'll get the thionamide before any iodine.

Give the ordered beta-blocker and fluids; hand off to the ICU.

collapse.headline: Collapse
collapse.body: High fever, a racing heart, agitation and GI symptoms in someone with Graves off treatment is thyroid storm: call for help, cool without aspirin, and get the beta-blocker in.

treated.headline: Treated
treated.body: You recognized thyroid storm and its trigger, called rapid response at once, cooled her without aspirin, didn't sedate and wait, and gave the beta-blocker. That is the expert path.

scoring.modelReasoning: Ms. Okoye has Graves disease, stopped her methimazole a month ago, and had surgery yesterday: two precipitants. A temperature over 40 C, a heart rate around 150 and irregular, agitation with new confusion, vomiting and diarrhea is thyroid storm, a true emergency with high mortality. Call the rapid response team now, cool her with blankets off, a cooling blanket and acetaminophen (not aspirin, which can raise free thyroid hormone), and don't sedate and wait. Give the ordered beta-blocker and fluids and transfer her to the ICU, where a thionamide comes before any iodine.
